title: Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf Warns 'Era of Proportionate Responses' to US Is Over
detail: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Sunday, September 6, 2026, that 'the era of proportionate responses' to US strikes 'is over,' warning any future violation of Iran's security would draw a 'faster, more intense and more painful response.' The threat followed Saturday's CENTCOM strikes sinking Iranian oil tankers, including the M/T Kylo, in retaliation for IRGC ballistic-missile attacks on two US Navy vessels. CENTCOM spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins dismissed Iran's claim of having struck a US vessel as a 'total lie,' while Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned, 'If Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers.' Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the administration remained open to nuclear negotiations with Tehran even as the sanctions and strikes campaign continued. President Trump again dismissed the six-month conflict as 'small potatoes' and defended VP Vance's reluctance to call it a war.

media.caption: Iran's economy and currency under strain as the war with the US enters its seventh month

title: Trump Administration Drafts Plan to Pay Married Stay-at-Home Parents Using Working-Parent Childcare Funds
detail: The Trump administration is drafting a rule, championed by Vice President JD Vance and incorporating legislative language Secretary of State Marco Rubio wrote as a senator, that would let married couples with one stay-at-home parent draw on the $12 billion Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF), a program created in the 1990s to help low- and moderate-income working parents afford childcare, according to a draft document reported Sunday, September 6, 2026. Under the proposal, a married couple in which one spouse works at least 35 hours a week and the other stays home could receive roughly $9,000 per child annually; unmarried couples and single non-working parents would not qualify. About 870,000 families currently receive CCDF subsidies, 80% of them single working parents (mostly mothers); some department lawyers have questioned the legality of a marriage requirement, and critics warn the change would redirect funds from working parents without new appropriations. The rule needs no congressional approval, requires White House sign-off and a public comment period, and could take effect as soon as 2027.

media.caption: VP JD Vance, the policy's chief champion, takes questions from reporters at the White House
